notes: Summary: Large mid-west regional bank; strong emphasis on Private VPC deployment and network-level isolation.

Primary ask: Private deployment behind customer VPC (no public internet exposure). Must support AWS PrivateLink or VPC peering (customer prefers PrivateLink for cross-account IAM boundaries, security prefers peering for predictable routing).

Network specifics: Require static egress IPs from Redwood side so bank can update bank firewall allowlist. Prefer flow: PrivateLink endpoint in customer account + AWS PrivateLink interface endpoints in Redwood-managed account. If peering: cross-account peering with route table entries; require documentation of IP ranges and route table changes.

Firewall / egress controls: Customer needs all egress via managed NAT/egress proxy under their control. No direct outbound to public IPs from inference nodes unless routed through customer's egress. Must provide list of destination IP ranges and FQDNs for allowlists.

IP allowlist: Will only allow calls from a defined set of /27 ranges. Redwood must provide CIDR lists for production and staging. Expect periodic rotation windows; need compatibility with bank change control calendar.

KMS/HSM: CMEK required. Integration with customer's AWS KMS key (cross-account grants) or HSM-backed keys via external KMS provider. Customer security team said 'keys must be under our control, Redwood cannot import keys' — implies use of cross-account grants + encryption-at-rest using customer-managed keys.

Audit logging & SIEM: All access logs, admin actions, and model invocation events must be exportable to customer's S3 (us-east-1) and forwarded to their Splunk/QRadar. Retention: 365 days for invocation logs; 7 years for audit trail metadata per compliance team.

Data residency: Production data must remain in US-only regions (us-east-1 / us-west-2). No replication to other regions without explicit approval. DR tests allowed but only in same region or secondary us-west-2 with signed agreement.
Compliance: SOC2 + ISO27001 evidence requested. They already run vendor SOC2 attestations; Redwood to provide SOC2 Type II report and recent pen-test summary.
Quote from CTO (call 2026-01-15): 'It cannot traverse the public internet. All inference traffic must terminate inside our VPC or via a PrivateLink endpoint.'
Quote from Head of Security: 'We need end-to-end key control, immutable audit logs, and the ability to revoke Redwood access immediately.'

POC scope notes: Short POC to validate PrivateLink connectivity, KMS cross-account grant flow, and audit log export to customer S3 + SIEM ingestion. POC success criteria: latency under 120ms p90 for 2048 tokens, successful CMEK decrypt/encrypt logs, and log ingestion into Splunk within 5 minutes.
Internal Redwood risks: Need SE to validate implementation pattern for PrivateLink vs peering; engineering to scope cost for dedicated NAT egress and static IPs.
Customer timeline: Wants production by 2026-05; procurement window Q2.

requirements_summary: Network: PrivateLink preferred; support for VPC peering as fallback. Clear CIDR ranges and interface endpoint guidance required.
Egress: All egress must flow through customer-managed NAT/proxy. Redwood should provide minimal destination list for allowlists.
Firewall rules: Bank will supply change window; Redwood to provide IPs and ports. TLS mutual auth for admin control plane preferred.
IP allowlists: Provide per-environment static IP blocks; scheduled rotation supported with 2 weeks notice.
KMS: Customer-managed keys (CMEK), cross-account grants, HSM compatibility. Key rotation policy: monthly automated rotation acceptable if controlled by customer.
Audit logging: Export syslogs, control plane events, and model invocation metadata to customer S3 (us-east-1) and stream to SIEM. Retention policies configurable.
Data residency: US-only; no replication to EU/APAC without written approval.
SLA/ops: 99.9% uptime required for production. Runbooks for incident response and immediate rollback/fallback to alternative model in case of regression.
Security docs: Need SOC2 Type II report, pen-test summary, architecture whitepaper for Private VPC deployment.
Business: Estimated ARR target 200k-500k; pricing sensitivity to unit token costs and egress-related engineering charges.
